'''Vasha''' was a [[Desert/Legends|desert]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] located in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']] [[Moddell sector/Legends|Moddell sector]]. It was the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the [[Insectoid/Legends|insectoid]] [[Vashan]] [[Species/Legends|species]], which governed itself through a system [[Theocracy|theocratic]] castes and members of which were prized as workers across the Moddell [[Sector/Legends|sector]]. After it experienced a series of religious wars that ended when contact was established with the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], Vasha came to be dominated by the [[Ayrou/Legends|Ayrou]] species from the planet [[Maya Kovel/Legends|Maya Kovel]], with Ayrou [[Administrator/Legends|administrators]] overseeing deep-delving [[Mining/Legends|mines]] from which Vashan [[Miner/Legends|miners]] retrieved valuable [[Ore/Legends|ores]] and [[Mineral/Legends|minerals]].

At some point by [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], miners in the mine known as [[The Abyss (Vasha)|The Abyss]] discovered the valuable [[Tessent|statue]] known as the [[Ayrou Tessent]]. When a group of [[Treasure hunting/Legends|treasure hunters]] subsequently visited The Abyss in order to retrieve the artifact, the Vashan theocrat [[Dochi At-Rial]] instead fled with the Tessent for a Vashan [[Inicus Mont|holy site]] situated on the [[Qina system/Legends|Qina system]] [[Moon/Legends|moon]] of the [[Qina/Legends|same name]].

==Description==
Vasha was a terrestrial [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="Endor" /> located in the [[Vasha system/Legends|Vasha system]]. It lay within the [[Inner Moddell systems]] area of<ref name="TEA" /> the [[Moddell sector/Legends|Moddell sector]],<ref name="EAOC Vasha" /> one of the [[Sector/Legends|subsectors]] making up the [[Inner Zuma Region]]<ref name="TEA" /> within the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']] [[Zuma sector/Legends|Zuma sector]].<ref name="EAOC Vasha" /> The [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]] known as the [[Annaj-Houche Run]] connected Vasha and the rest of the Vasha [[Star system/Legends|system]] to the [[Maya Kovel system/Legends|Maya Kovel system]] as well as [[Houche system/Legends|Houche system]]<ref name="TEA" /> in the [[Sugai sector/Legends|Sugai sector]],<ref name="EAOC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}}</ref> while another [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] route linked it to the [[Vex system/Legends|Vex system]].<ref name="TEA" />

Vasha's [[local year]] lasted 402 [[Local day/Legends|local days]], each of which was twenty-two [[Standard hour/Legends|standard hours]] long. Its [[Gravity/Legends|gravity]] was 110% standard, and it had a breathable Type I [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]] and a [[Temperature/Legends|hot]] climate. [[Desert/Legends|Desert]] dominated the planet's surface,<ref name="Endor" /> although its terrain also included lonely, craggy [[Mountain/Legends|mountains]]. The [[Ore/Legends|ore]] veins situated close to rocky Vasha's core held vast [[Mineral/Legends|wealth]]. The planet's depths were [[Homeworld/Legends|home]] to [[apilid worm]]s, [[Meter/Legends|meter]]-long [[Diet/Legends|predators]] with mandibles that bore through solid rock and metal. Prior to their discovery in the [[Mining/Legends|mine]] known as [[The Abyss (Vasha)|The Abyss]], apilid [[Worm/Legends|worms]] had not been previously encountered by the inhabitants of Vasha.<ref name="Tessent" />

==History==
By the [[Time/Legends|time]] the Inner Zuma Region saw its first visits by [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] [[Colonist/Legends|settlers]], Vasha's native [[Vashan]]s, who were divided into rival [[Theocracy|theocratical]] castes, were engaged in a series of religious wars. Once contact was established with the Republic, the wars ended, but Vasha eventually became a virtual satrapy of the [[Ayrou/Legends|Ayrou]] [[Species/Legends|species]] from the planet [[Maya Kovel/Legends|Maya Kovel]].<ref name="Endor" /> At some point, the [[Vashan Liberation Force]], a group of approximately twenty Vashans intent on organizing a revolt against the Ayrou, was formed on [[Sarafur]],<ref name="Tessent" /> a world in the [[Kuna's Tail system/Legends|Kuna's Tail system]].<ref name="Endor" />

{{RPG|"[[Race for the Tessent]]"}}
[[File:Vashan2.jpg|thumb|left|300px|On Vasha, a group of treasure hunters confronted the Vashans [[Dochi At-Rial]] and [[Poina Tuc-shol]] (pictured).]]
At some point by [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]],<ref name="3 ABY">By default, the events of {{GamerCite|9|Race for the Tessent}} are set during the opposition to [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] [[Slavery/Legends|slavery]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]]. ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' dates the events of [[Star Wars (1977) 69|''Star Wars'' (1977) 69]], which depict the [[Battle of the City of Bone|end]] of the Imperial presence on Mandalore per {{InsiderCite|80|The History of the Mandalorians: Exploring the Evolution of a Mighty Race of Warriors}}, to [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]].</ref> Vashan [[Miner/Legends|miners]] in the mine known as The Abyss discovered the [[Ayrou Tessent]], a [[Chalcedony/Legends|chalcedony]] idol that was one of the [[Alsakan Tessent|two]] [[Tessent]] artifacts and that, according to a legend, held encoded coordinates for a treasure vault the [[Ur-Chapterhouse]] of the Ayrou ''[[il Madri]]'' religious tradition of Maya Kovel had hidden in one of the [[Kuna systems]]. Eventually, a group of [[Treasure hunting/Legends|treasure hunters]] visited The Abyss after learning about the find through rumors and obtaining a hint as to the visual appearance of [[Dochi At-Rial]], a Vashan caste theocrat who had the Tessent in [[Gender/Legends|his]] possession. In The Abyss, the group confronted both At-Rial and the Vashan [[Sword/Legends|swordsman]] [[Poina Tuc-shol]]&mdash;who, due to religious reasons, was wary of any non-Vashans obtaining the Tessent and had thus shadowed the treasure [[Hunting/Legends|hunters]] throughout their stay on the planet&mdash;but the former managed to flee with the Tessent for the Vashan holy site of [[Inicus Mont]] on the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Qina/Legends|Qina]]<ref name="Tessent" /> in the [[Qina system/Legends|Qina system]].<ref name="TEA" />
{{Endgame}}

==Inhabitants==
{{Main|Vashan}}
Vasha was the homeworld of the Vashans, a species of powerful and tireless [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]]<ref name="Endor" /> [[Insectoid/Legends|insectoids]]<ref name="Tessent" /> who spoke the [[Vashan (language)|Vashan]] [[Language/Legends|language]]. Although the Vashans were prized as workers across the Moddell sector, they were also loathed for their odd habits involving their six [[Stomach/Legends|antestomaches]]<ref name="Endor" /> as well as their unusual [[Vashan religion|religious]] practices.<ref name="Tessent" />

By the time of the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], Vasha was home to one billion Vashans as well as two hundred thousand Ayrou. The Vashans, whose society was organized into theocratic castes, had access to [[Realspace/Legends|space]]-[[Technology level|level]] technology. Each [[Standard year/Legends|year]], around two million highest-ranking members of all Vashan castes went on a pilgrimage to the moon Qina,<ref name="Endor" /> [[Transport/Legends|transported]] between Vasha and Qina by multiple [[Freighter/Legends|freighters]] that arrived on the moon every hour.<ref name="Tessent" />

==Locations==
Vasha featured ore mines<ref name="Endor" /> that reached nearly into the very core of the planet, where the Vashan religion stated that the realm of the [[Rot-Maggot]], the Vashan [[Deity/Legends|god]] of decay, lay. The mining facilities were controlled by Ayrou [[Administrator/Legends|administrators]] based out of<ref name="Tessent" /> a patchwork of [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceports]]&mdash;two [[Stellar-class starport|stellar-class]] and ten [[Standard Class starport|standard-class]]&mdash;on Vasha's surface.<ref name="Endor" /> Railing-less [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]] platforms took miners from the planet's surface into its deepest mine, which was known locally as The Abyss and was at one point lost.<ref name="Tessent" />

Vasha's primary spaceport, [[Tatarrar]], was located near The Abyss, and it contained both [[Cantina/Legends|drinking-dens]] as well as honeycomb-shaped dormitories, which were situated outside the spaceport and where Vashan miners [[Sleep/Legends|slept]]. In addition, traditional Vashan combat schools were hidden in the planet's mountains.<ref name="Tessent" />

==Behind the scenes==
Vasha first appeared in the [[Roleplaying game|roleplaying]] adventure "[[Race for the Tessent]]," which was published for use with [[Wizards of the Coast]]'s ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'' in the [[Star Wars Gamer 9|ninth issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars Gamer]]'' magazine<ref name="Tessent" /> on [[February 22]], [[2002]].<ref name="GamerDate">{{SWArchive|url=gaming/other/rpg/news20020222.html|text=Starfighters Soar in Gamer #9}}</ref> The [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' placed Vasha in grid square H-16.<ref name="TEA" />

[[File:Race_for_the_Tessent_G9.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Vasha was introduced as one of the settings in the roleplaying adventure "Race for the Tessent."]]
Instead of featuring a set plot, "Race for the Tessent" presents several settings in the Moddell sector, Vasha being one of them, that the player characters may visit during their search for one of the two artifacts known as the Tessents. For each of the settings, the adventure also suggests possible circumstances for a Tessent being hidden there. This article assumes that as much of the non-contradictory information presented in the adventure as possible is [[canon]]ical with respect to the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity. Therefore, it is assumed that the Ayrou Tessent was hidden on Vasha and that the player characters visit The Abyss, where they confront both Dochi At-Rial and Poina Tuc-shol. At-Rial is assumed to have then fled to Qina with the Tessent.<ref name="Tessent" />

"Race for the Tessent" suggests that, instead of descending into The Abyss, the player characters may alternately explore the Vashan dormitories outside the Tatarrar spaceport, where At-Rial has possibly placed the Tessent in his sleeping cell. If the player characters attempt to confront At-Rial anywhere else but in The Abyss, the theocrat immediately escapes to Qina with the artifact. On the other hand, if they are successful in retrieving&mdash;either through intimidation or a bribe&mdash;the Tessent during the confrontation in The Abyss, At-Rial attempts to have Tuc-shol try and gain the idol back. If the player characters arrive after one of their rival parties has already acquired the Tessent on Vasha, the planet descends into complete chaos as the Vashans, who view their discovery of the Tessent as a sign of divine favor, channel their outrage into a revolt targeting their Ayrou overseers and any other non-Vashans present. Finally, if the player characters don't visit Vasha at all, they can still be drawn to Qina by rumors that Vashan miners have uncovered the idol and [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttled]] it to the moon for safekeeping it at Inicus Mont.<ref name="Tessent" />
